From these preliminary results, we
see three main priorities. The first one
is that we need to reduce the amount of manual work involving preparing
metadata and submitting data.
Secondly, we need better metadata validation and clearer
guidance on repository requirements so people can identify
problems early and know how to fix them before submission.
Third, we need to test interoperable workflow components
with the people who actually use the tools and make sure that the tool
is fit for real publication practices.
So the main message for this talk is that making
marine eDNA data fair is not only about the technology, but
it is also about making the publication process clear,
practical, and manageable for the people who are doing the work.
